title: Camunda 7 refuses to deploy a process model that does not declare when its history will be deleted
content:
From the history-cleanup documentation: *"The history time to live is mandatory, any deployment or re-deployment of any model resource (BPMN, DMN, CMMN) that contains a historyTimeToLive of null will be prevented."*

Cleanup itself is opt-in — no cleanup window is configured by default, so nothing is actually removed until an administrator schedules it. But the declaration is compulsory: you cannot deploy a process without stating a date on which its history becomes disposable.

It is a revealing design choice. The engine treats process history as operational data with a lifespan, to the point of refusing work that declines to specify one. That is a coherent position for an orchestrator and an incompatible one for a system of record.
description: historyTimeToLive is mandatory, and any deployment containing a null value is prevented — the engine will not accept a model intended to keep a permanent record.
